items.prompt: Two tabs load revision 0. Tab A saves and releases the Web Lock; tab B then acquires it with a draft based on revision 0. What stops B from overwriting A's change?
items.answer: Inside the lock, save sees stored text differs from B's baseline and throws a conflict
distractors: The Web Lock itself refuses B, because tab A was the most recent holder of the lock
B's revision 0 is lower than the stored revision 1, so validateState rejects the draft
Nothing does: the last tab to save wins, which the guide documents as intended behavior
items.explanation: A lock serializes cooperating saves but does not know what each draft was based on; the baseline comparison (compare-and-set) of the current raw text against the text remembered when B's draft began does.

items.prompt: Another tool rewrites the storage key with the same revision number but different content. Does a draft started before that write still save?
items.answer: No: the raw strings are compared, so any change at all makes the baseline stale
distractors: Yes: only the revision numbers are compared, and the two numbers still match
Yes: the parsed boards are deep-compared and the two category lists are merged
Only if the other tool also held the Web Lock while it rewrote the storage key
items.explanation: Comparing raw text rather than a parsed field means no write can slip past the check by preserving one number, even one leaving revision unchanged.

items.prompt: An imported board file claims revision: 999 and is saved onto empty storage. What revision is committed?
items.answer: 1: the revision is recomputed as the current stored revision plus one
distractors: 999: validateState accepts any safe integer revision and keeps it as is
1000: the imported revision plus one, since each save increments it
0: imported files always reset the revision, so the count restarts
items.explanation: Revision is derived, not trusted: { ...normalized, revision: revision + 1 }, where revision comes from current storage (0 when empty), and the spread overwrites the candidate's revision.

items.prompt: setItem throws because storage is full while the learner saves an edited board. What does the learner see?
items.answer: An error, with the proposal still in the dialog and the accepted board unchanged
distractors: The edited board on screen, which then disappears again the next time the page loads
An empty board, since the failed setItem call already cleared the storage key
The edited board, which was saved to sessionStorage as a fallback location
items.explanation: current is replaced only after store.save succeeds. A draft is a proposal; the saved board is accepted state. Updating the screen before persistence succeeds is the classic CRUD bug this avoids.

items.prompt: The learner deletes a question that was already marked used. What happens to usedQuestionIds?
items.answer: removeQuestion filters out exactly that id; the other markers stay correct
distractors: Every marker shifts down one position so it keeps following the array order
The markers are all kept, and validation later repairs the dangling one
All used markers are cleared to avoid leaving any inconsistent board state
items.explanation: The markers store question ids, not positions. Stable ids distinguish records from positions, so deleting the first question cannot make its marker refer to the former second question.

items.prompt: An imported board gives a category and one of its questions the same id 'x'. Does validateState accept it?
items.answer: No: one shared claim set covers both kinds, so the second 'x' is a duplicate
distractors: Yes: category ids and question ids are claimed in separate namespaces
Yes: only question ids need to be unique, since they alone key the used markers
No, but only because 'x' is shorter than the minimum allowed id length
items.explanation: One claim() set covers both record kinds and throws 'Duplicate record identity.', so an id is unique across the whole board.

items.prompt: The stored board is malformed JSON. What does the app do on load?
items.answer: It keeps the raw text for download and shows examples with editing disabled
distractors: It silently overwrites the stored key with the example board and carries on
It deletes the corrupt key and starts the learner with an empty question bank
It crashes with an uncaught SyntaxError from JSON.parse and shows a blank page
items.explanation: parseState throws, valid becomes false, the raw text is kept, and the examples render with tiles and editing disabled. Nothing is written until the user explicitly chooses replacement, and the raw text can be exported first.

items.prompt: With replaceInvalid: true, which check is excused - and which still runs?
items.answer: Only parsing the corrupt stored value is excused; the baseline check still runs
distractors: Both the baseline comparison and the parse of the corrupt stored value are skipped
Candidate validation is excused so examples save; the parse still runs
The Web Lock is excused, as recovery is single-tab; the parse still runs
items.explanation: The baseline comparison runs before the parse, so an old recovery screen cannot overwrite a newer repair. Recovery refuses to overwrite unreadable data without both confirmation and a matching baseline.

items.prompt: A category name contains . Validation accepts it. Why does it not execute?
items.answer: The renderer sets textContent, so the value is shown as literal text
distractors: validateState strips angle brackets from every category and question name
The CSP blocks the image from loading, so its onerror handler never fires
Browsers never run inline event handlers on elements inside an h2 heading
items.explanation: textContent is never parsed as HTML. Validation and safe rendering are different defences; the CSP is a second layer, not the primary one.

items.prompt: The learner double-clicks Save. What prevents a second concurrent save?
items.answer: The first click disables every control, so the second hits a disabled button
distractors: The Web Lock queues the second save, which then fails as a stale-baseline conflict
The browser debounces double-clicks on form buttons automatically
Nothing does: both saves run, and the second overwrites the first one
items.explanation: save() disables every button, input and textarea before awaiting; `if (busy) return false` is defence in depth for programmatic calls. The ignored attempt shows no message - finding 6 notes this silent no-op could confuse a future caller.

items.prompt: A clue dialog is open when another tab starts a new round. The learner clicks Mark used. What happens?
items.answer: It conflicts ('This board changed in another tab'), since it uses the dialog's baseline
distractors: The clue is marked used, and the other tab's new round is lost from storage
The clue is marked used on top of the other tab's new round automatically
The dialog closes silently, without saving anything or showing any error
items.explanation: The save is checked against clue.raw, captured when the dialog opened, so it is safe but conservative. It cannot resurrect old progress, but the user must close and reopen the clue; rebasing compatible changes would need its own test.

items.prompt: Is the answer secret until the learner clicks 'Reveal answer'?
items.answer: No: showClue puts the answer in a hidden element, readable in devtools
distractors: Yes: the answer is fetched from the server only when Reveal is clicked
Yes: the answer stays encrypted in storage until the learner reveals it
Yes: the CSP stops devtools from reading the contents of hidden elements
items.explanation: showClue writes question.answer into the answer element and only sets hidden; hidden is presentation, not secrecy. Fine for a local study tool; any multi-user version must omit protected fields from what it sends.

items.front: Which invariant must survive any framework change in front of BoardStore (test/store.test.js:106-119)?
items.back: Two cooperating savers sharing one baseline produce exactly one winner and one revision: Promise.allSettled shows 1 fulfilled and 1 rejected save, and the stored revision is 1.

items.front: In BoardStore.save (store.js:51-59), what does deleting line 53 break, and why would removing the lock on line 51 instead still leave a window?
items.back: Without line 53 (the baseline compare) tab B overwrites tab A. Without the lock, lines 52-59 still run uninterrupted within one tab (no await), but tabs may run in separate processes and localStorage has no atomic read-modify-write across them, so two compare-then-write sequences can interleave.

items.front: store.js:53 compares the whole serialized board. Why should a reviewer not flag 'two tabs editing different questions conflict' as a bug?
items.back: Whole-board CAS is coarse by design and documented as a limit. Fixing it needs per-record versions (e.g. a server database with conditional updates), which is a later exercise - not a tweak to this comparison.

items.front: Senior-review finding 1: validation in store.js:20-21 throws 'Points must be...' or 'Prompt must contain...'. What is missing and how would you fix it?
items.back: The message does not identify the record, so repairing a 2 MiB import means hunting. The validator already has category and question indices in scope inside its map callbacks; include them (and the category name) in the thrown message.
